_readme: Reasoned allowlist for legitimate changes to files listed in apps/web/frozen-files.json's "files" section. Each entry: { file, new_hash, reason, approved }. A legitimate future change bumps the hash in frozen-files.json AND adds a matching entry here in the same PR, so a reviewer sees the intent. NOTE: this allowlist mechanism does NOT apply to frozen-files.json's "room_status_values" section -- room-status token VALUE changes have no allowlist escape (see FROZEN.md).

entries.reason: Additive only: added an Avatar primitive (getInitials/getAvatarColor, previously inlined ad hoc in Header/Sidebar) and new StatusDot tone key aliases ('alert', 'info', 'caution') mapping to the same already-frozen --alert/--info/--caution CSS vars previously only reachable via the 'dirty'/'clean'/'pickup' tone keys. No existing exports, prop shapes, or room-status color values changed.

Assign-mode redesign (imported Claude Design 'Assign mode - room board'): added unassigned/staged quick-filter chips next to the existing DEP/FULL/LIGHT chips (assignFilter prop threaded through StatusSummaryBar), and a per-floor bulk-assign button in the floor header (restructured the header from one <button> into a flex row so the new bulk-assign <button> isn't nested inside the collapse-toggle button). No existing exports, room-status color/token values, or non-assign-mode rendering changed.

Two follow-up fixes to the assign-mode Remove flow, both retroactively added to this allowlist (the hash bump for the first fix was missed at commit time -- this entry covers both): (1) a room assigned only via the room_status.assigned_to mirror (no room_assignments row for today, assignment_id null) now renders as 'Assigned' whenever it belongs to the active housekeeper, instead of silently falling back to looking unassigned -- relaxed isSavedAssignedToActive to not require a backing assignment id, and added an onRemoveMirroredAssignment prop for that no-id case. (2) closed a race window where clicking Remove immediately after Save (while assignment_id is still the `optimistic-${roomId}` placeholder from the save's optimistic cache update) silently no-op'd instead of deleting the just-persisted assignment -- the Remove button is now disabled and shows 'Saving...' until the real id lands. No existing exports, room-status color/token values, or non-assign-mode rendering changed.

Companion to the RoomCard.tsx entry above (mirror-assignment fix, hash bump also missed at commit time): added handleRemoveMirroredAssignment (optimistic cache clear of assigned_to + call to the new DELETE /housekeeping/room-assignment/{room_id} endpoint) and wired it as RoomCard's onRemoveMirroredAssignment prop. No existing exports, room-status color/token values, or non-assign-mode rendering changed.

Follow-up 2: the assigned-housekeeper row and AI note were never populating because the board endpoint returns assigned_to (UUID) + prediction but NOT user_profiles, and the drawer read room.user_profiles for the name. Now the drawer resolves the housekeeper name from room.assigned_to via the shared ['staff-list'] roster (staffApi.list, already cached by the boards so no extra request), so the housekeeper row renders on every surface. The AI note relies on room.prediction, which the board only returns when include_predictions=true — SimplifiedDashboard was calling getBoard(..., false) so its rooms carried no prediction; that call is flipped to true in the same change (RoomStatusBoard/EngineeringRoomBoard already pass true). No exports or the Props contract changed. Follow-up 1: departure rooms with no explicit checkout_time now display the standard 11:00 AM checkout (DEFAULT_CHECKOUT_TIME) in the drawer's departure row instead of 'No checkout time set'; staff can still push it later via the Change departure sheet. Display-only default, nothing persisted until the sheet writes a real time. Prior context: strict re-import of Claude Design 'Room Drawer.dc.html' (Hotel dashboard unified interface project, 09e1c367). The user asked to remove every earlier drawer frontend and see ONLY the Claude mock, and explicitly chose 'strict design only' over keeping the extra features. So the render tree was reduced to exactly the mock's structure: the status-colored hero header (Instrument Serif room number, floor/room-type subtitle, live elapsed/base_clean_minutes progress bar while IN_PROGRESS), guest+housekeeper hairline avatar rows (VIP as a right-tag on the guest row, not a header star), a fact-row group ('Checkout'/'Departure' change-departure row + 'Open work orders' row), a single unboxed violet 'AI note' (real room_readiness_prediction, still gated to non-housekeepers), the sticky footer (real primary state-machine action + message-housekeeping composer via notificationsApi.sendDirect + report-issue), and the 'Change departure' bottom sheet (late-checkout chips -> real handleSaveCheckoutTime, 'Convert to stayover' -> real handleMarkStayover). DELETED, per the user's explicit strict-design choice, the previously-kept extras that the mock has no place for: the Add Note form, the Lost & Found action + LogFoundItemModal, the Departure-checkout box (mark-checked-out/undo), the OOO WO info block, the Active Guest Requests list, the Open Tasks list, the Last Clean evidence block, and the expandable Room History timeline (plus their queries: room-history, room-work-orders, room-clean-sessions, room-guest-requests, room-tasks, clean-session, and the guestRequests/tasks/cleanSessions API imports). Mutations now surface via the existing toast instead of inline success/error banners, matching the mock's single-toast affordance. The 'Next arrival' mock row is still omitted (no reservation-ahead data model exists). All header/status colors still reuse the hash-frozen room-status CSS vars (--alert/--progress/--caution/--ready/--info/--blocked) verbatim -- no room-status token value changed. No exports or the Props contract ({ room, isOpen, onClose, onCheckoutTimeSaved }) changed, so RoomStatusBoard/housekeeping pages/EngineeringRoomBoard call sites are unaffected. Supersedes the prior 'Wave 1/Wave 2' entry for this file.
entries.reason_superseded_note: PRIOR REASON (kept for history): Imported Claude Design 'Simplified Dashboard' then 'Room Drawer' (Hotel dashboard unified interface project) restyle of the drawer to the terracotta/paper v2 visual language, requested twice by the user with the second pass explicitly asking for an exact copy of the dedicated Room Drawer mock. Wave 1: status-colored hero header (room number in Instrument Serif, floor/room-type subtitle, elapsed-time bar + real base_clean_minutes average while IN_PROGRESS, capped at 720min to avoid a stale-timestamp bogus reading -- bug-1234) replacing the old thin top-bar + plain header; guest/housekeeper hairline avatar rows and hairline fact rows (in/out/checked-out/late-checkout/open-WO) replacing the old 'Assigned to X' text block; the AI Prediction card restyled unboxed with a violet 'AI NOTE' label (risk-level color/icon preserved on the lead-in); and a 'Change departure' bottom sheet (late-checkout time chips 12/1/2/4/Other + existing real handleSaveCheckoutTime, and the existing real handleMarkStayover as the 'Convert to stayover' alt row) replacing the raw inline time-input editor. Wave 2 (exact-copy pass): matched the mock's header eyebrow copy precisely ('Stayover · guest in house' for occupied, 'Checkout · assigned' vs 'Checkout · due out' for departures keyed off real assignedName presence instead of clean-status), and added the mock's sticky footer (primary action + message-housekeeping + report-issue, all real: primary is a room-status state machine mapped onto the app's actual VALID_TRANSITIONS-backed roomsApi.updateStatus -- Queue for inspection/Mark inspected/Start clean/Request clean/Return to service, each role-gated server-side, with an honest no-op toast only for 'Hold for arrival' on already-INSPECTED rooms exactly as the mock itself does for its no-op vacant case; message-housekeeping opens a real composer using notificationsApi.sendDirect against room.assigned_to, falling back to a toast when no housekeeper is assigned rather than fabricating a recipient; report-issue scrolls to and opens the existing real work-order form). Deliberately did NOT add the mock's fake 'Next arrival' row or its arrival-conflict-aware AI-note/sheet-note text -- no reservation-ahead data model exists in this app, so that specific row/logic was omitted rather than fabricated (existing 'Open work orders' row is the only drawerRows entry kept, since it's real). Did NOT remove the pre-existing, more-capable Add Note / Work Order / Lost & Found action grid or the Departure checkout (manual mark-checked-out/undo/stayover) card, both real functionality with no equivalent in the demo mock -- keeping them is a deliberate non-regression call, not an oversight. All header/status colors still reuse the existing hash-frozen room-status CSS vars (--alert/--progress/--caution/--ready/--info/--blocked) verbatim -- no room-status token value changed. New UI copy added to both en.ts and es.ts (parity verified via check-i18n-parity.mjs, 1712 keys). No exports or the Props contract ({ room, isOpen, onClose, onCheckoutTimeSaved }) changed, so RoomStatusBoard/housekeeping pages/EngineeringRoomBoard call sites are unaffected.

entries.reason: Live-bind the open RoomDetailDrawer to the board's auto-refetching room list. selectedRoom was a frozen snapshot captured at click time, so a drawer mutation (checkout time, status, assignment) did not appear until the drawer was closed and reopened. Added a derived `drawerRoom = { ...selectedRoom, ...(allRooms.find by room_id) }` and passed it to RoomDetailDrawer instead of the raw selectedRoom, so every refetch/invalidation flows straight into the open drawer. Additive only: no exports, room-status color/token values, or existing rendering changed; the same reactivity fix was applied in parallel to the non-frozen SimplifiedDashboard.tsx and housekeeping/rooms/page.tsx drawer hosts.

For an OCCUPIED room (guest in house), the primary footer button was 'Request clean', which jumped the room straight to IN_PROGRESS with no housekeeper assigned -- a dead end nobody would know to act on. Replaced it, for front_desk/supervisor/GM only (canAssignClean = canSupervise || role === 'front_desk'), with 'Assign room clean', which opens a new bottom sheet (same pattern as the existing Change departure sheet) letting the caller pick a stayover clean type (Full/Light, from CLEAN_TYPE_OPTIONS minus Departure) and a housekeeper in one screen, then calls the existing housekeepingApi.saveAssignments (same endpoint the Routes page's Publish flow uses) with room_id + housekeeper_id + clean_type -- the backend already derives the correct room_status (PICKUP) from clean_type, so no separate status-advance call is needed. Housekeepers in the sheet are ranked by route fit via a new rankHousekeepers() helper: fetches today's open board rooms (new light query, includePredictions=false, only enabled while the sheet is open) and scores each housekeeper by whether they already have open rooms in the same building as the target room (best -- continues their route with no courtyard crossing), then floor distance within that building, then an idle housekeeper with no rooms yet (middle tier), then a housekeeper currently working the other building (worst tier, discouraged not blocked), with current workload (credits) as a final tiebreak -- mirrors the building-first sort already added to HousekeepingRoutes.tsx. The top-ranked housekeeper is pre-selected and shown with a 'Suggested' badge; the caller can still pick anyone else in the ranked list. Non-target roles (housekeeper, engineer, chief_engineer) keep the exact prior 'Request clean' -> IN_PROGRESS behavior unchanged. New i18n keys added to both en.ts/es.ts under housekeeping.roomDetail.primary.assignRoomClean and a new housekeeping.roomDetail.assignClean.* block (parity verified via check-i18n-parity.mjs). Companion backend change: POST /housekeeping/assignments' require_role widened from (gm, housekeeping_supervisor) to also include front_desk, since this is the only way for front_desk to reach that endpoint (per-room/per-housekeeper tenant ownership is still enforced server-side via _ensure_tenant_row/_ensure_housekeeper) -- mirrors the existing front_desk grant on checkout-time/stayover writes in this same file. No exports or the Props contract ({ room, isOpen, onClose, onCheckoutTimeSaved }) changed, so all drawer host call sites are unaffected.

PICKUP status only ever means a stayover clean (Full or Light) is queued, but the header eyebrow just said 'Pickup' with no way to tell which type without opening the guest row (which is only rendered when guestName is present, and even then just says the clean type once under the guest's name, not tied to the header state). Added pickupCleanTypeShort = status === 'PICKUP' ? getCleanTypeShortLabel(room?.clean_type) : null and appended it to the header eyebrow line as ' · Full' / ' · Light', unconditionally visible whenever the room is in Pickup regardless of whether a guest name is on file. Additive only: no exports, room-status color/token values, or non-pickup rendering changed.

A departure room (clean_type === 'DEP') whose guest was still in-house (effective status === 'OCCUPIED', per getEffectiveRoomStatusForCleanType in cleanType.ts) rendered identically to one already vacated -- both got the amber 'caution' header with an assignment-based label ('Checkout · assigned' / 'Checkout · due out'), with no visual distinction for 'guest hasn't left yet' vs 'guest is gone, room needs the departure clean'. getHeaderTone's DEPARTURE branch now checks status itself: still-occupied departures get the red 'alert' tone striped (same visual treatment as an occupied stayover, since a guest is physically in the room) with eyebrow 'Occupied departure'; vacated departures get the same red 'alert' tone unstriped with eyebrow 'Vacant departure'. Dropped the now-unused isAssigned parameter from getHeaderTone (and the call site's `!!assignedName` argument) since the branch no longer keys off assignment. Removed the now-dead checkoutAssigned/checkoutDueOut i18n keys and added occupiedDeparture/vacantDeparture in both en.ts/es.ts (parity verified via check-i18n-parity.mjs). Companion non-frozen change: SimplifiedDashboard.tsx's 'Departures · checkout' stat tile was relabeled to 'Departures' and its dot recolored from --caution (amber) to --alert (red), to match the same red-for-departures convention. getOccupancy()/showDepartureRow/departureRowLabel/departureRowValue and the fact-row 'Checkout'/'Departure' text are unchanged -- this only touches the header color/eyebrow, not which rooms count as departures or the departure fact row's own copy. No exports or the Props contract changed.

getOccupancy() only checked room.status === 'OCCUPIED', so a PICKUP-status room (a stayover clean queued while the guest is still physically in the room) fell through to 'VACANT' -- wrong, since the guest hasn't left. Added `|| room?.status === 'PICKUP'` to the OCCUPIED branch, matching the equivalent fix in SimplifiedDashboard.tsx's classifyOccupancy() (which this function's comment already says it mirrors) so 'Vacant' only ever means nobody is in the room on both surfaces. Because getHeaderTone's `occupancy === 'OCCUPIED'` branch previously ran before its `status === 'PICKUP'` branch, this would have overwritten the Pickup-specific header (added in a prior change: 'PICKUP · FULL'/'PICKUP · LIGHT') with the generic 'STAYOVER · GUEST IN HOUSE' label -- reordered getHeaderTone so the `status === 'PICKUP'` check runs first (right after the IN_PROGRESS/OOO checks) and wins, so the pickup header is unchanged. The only observable effect of the occupancy fix is that showDepartureRow/departureRowLabel/departureRowValue (which read occupancy, not status) now correctly show a 'Departure: Tomorrow' fact row for Pickup rooms too, same as any other stayover-occupied room, instead of hiding it. No exports or the Props contract changed.
